section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Body Esteem Scale (BES; Franzoi & Shields, 1984), a 35-item measure where participants rate feelings about body parts and functions on a 5-point scale. It details three subscales (physical/sexual attractiveness, upper body strength/weight concern, and physical condition) with reported internal consistency (alphas) for women and men. section_summary.evidence_source:
Body Esteem Scale (BES; Franzoi & Shields, 1984)
This is a 35-item scale in which participants are asked to rate their feelings about various body parts and functions. For both women and men, three subscales are computed, namely (1) physical attractiveness (PA) for men (in the present study, a = .89) or sexual attractiveness (SA) for women (a = .82); (2) upper body strength (UBS) for men (a = .86) or weight concern (WC) for women (a = .87), and (3) physical condition (PC) for both women (a = .80) and men (a = .89).
